Rishikesh, Uttarakhand: Continuous rainfall in the Garhwal region and Dehradun district has pushed the Ganga River in Rishikesh 15 centimetres above the danger mark.  The administration has placed the area on high alert and is cautioning people through loudspeakers at major ghats along the river to prevent any untoward incident. The State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), Jal Police and Rishikesh Police have also been deployed on alert at the Ganga ghats.  Authorities are closely monitoring the situation as rainfall continues across the region.  #TheSentinel #Rishikesh #Uttarakhand

ACIDRE: CONGRESS MUST EXAMINE SCHOOL SAFETY AFTER ZAMBOANGA SHOOTING  House Committee on Higher and Technical Education Chairperson and TINGOG Party-list Rep. Jude Acidre expressed grief over the Ateneo de Zamboanga University shooting, which killed two students and injured several others.  Acidre said the incident, following the Tacloban school shooting last June, should prompt Congress to examine gaps in school safety, mental health and psychosocial support, guidance and counseling, crisis response, and access to firearms.  He stressed that lawmakers should listen to students, parents, teachers, counselors, school administrators, and communities in crafting stronger safeguards.  "Every parent should be able to send a child to school in the morning with the confidence that he or she will come home safely. Every student should be able to walk into a classroom without fear."  @News5PH

Five senior officials from the Uganda Registration Services Bureau (@URSBHQ ) have been placed on mandatory leave as of August 14, 2026, amid a corruption probe involving allegations of financial impropriety, abuse of office, and mismanagement.  Affected are Registrar General Mercy Kainobwisho, Commissioner for Business Registration Gilbert Agaba, Assistant Commissioner Walid Kule, ICT Commissioner Arthur Kwesiga, and Deputy Registrar General for Finance Alex Anganya.  The move follows President @KagutaMuseveni 's July 24 directive for an audit after internal whistleblower complaints, including from Agaba, about inflated ICT contracts, money laundering via the Non-Individual Register project, and revenue under-collection.  President Museveni suspended top URSB officials including Registrar General Mercy Kainobwisho over whistleblower allegations of embezzlement, inflated ICT contracts, money laundering, irregular procurements, and revenue shortfalls.  This quotes Museveni's letter directing the Inspector General of Government to lead investigations with State House auditors Kawawa and Tumwine while placing the officials on leave pending a forensic audit. This also highlights infighting among URSB managers and governance failures at the bureau, whose headquarters is shown in the attached aerial photo of the distinctive curved building in Kampala.  No findings from the Museveni-ordered forensic audit of the Uganda Registration Services Bureau (URSB) have been publicly released as of August 18, 2026.  The audit is ongoing. Forensic auditors were active at URSB headquarters in Kampala for several days before five senior officials were placed on mandatory leave around August 14, 2026. URSB confirmed the exercise on August 17, stating it is being conducted “in accordance with established procedures and applicable laws,” with service delivery remaining uninterrupted. Further details are to be provided “where appropriate” after the processes conclude.  Background prompting the audit President Yoweri Museveni’s July 24, 2026 directive ordered key officials (including Registrar General Mercy Kainobwisho and others) on leave pending the audit into alleged embezzlement of government funds, abuse of office, money laundering, maladministration, and institutional mismanagement. He directed the Inspector General of Government to lead the investigations, assisted by State House auditors.  The move followed complaints by Commissioner for Business Registration Gilbert Agaba (who was also placed on leave). Agaba alleged issues including inflation of ICT system contracts, money laundering linked to the Non-Individual Register project, embezzlement/misappropriation of funds, irregular procurements, fraudulent registrations, weak internal financial controls, and revenue under-collection. These remain allegations and have not been independently proven.  Prior related audit findings (not the current forensic audit) Earlier Auditor General reports (covering periods up to around 2024/2025) had already flagged problems at URSB, such as: Weaknesses in the Online Business Registration System (OBRS, costing ~UGX 6.5 billion), including inadequate controls against fraudulent filings/forged signatures, system outages, and data privacy gaps (e.g., unredacted personal information shared). Issues with the Security Interest in Movable Property Registry System (SIMPRS).  Accumulation of domestic arrears, limited competition in some procurements, and other operational/financial control weaknesses. These earlier findings provide context for the governance and systems concerns but are distinct from the current forensic audit ordered by the President.  Forensic audits of this nature typically take time to complete and publish results (often weeks to months). Check official channels such as URSB statements, the Inspectorate of Government, or major Ugandan news outlets for any future releases. The Online Business Registration System (OBRS) of the Uganda Registration Services Bureau (URSB) has faced significant documented flaws, primarily detailed in the Auditor General’s report covering the period up to around late 2025 (with findings publicly reported in early 2026). OBRS was launched in December 2022 after roughly three years of design, development, and maintenance work. URSB invested approximately UGX 6.49 billion (about Shs 6.5 billion) in the system, which was intended to modernize and speed up business registration processes (name reservation, incorporation, amendments, data updates, etc.) as part of broader digital transformation efforts.  Key System Flaws Identified by the Auditor General Weak fraud prevention and authentication controls: The system cannot properly authenticate digital signatures or verify that approvals/submissions come from legitimate company owners. Fraudulent filings (including forged signatures and unauthorized entries) are typically only addressed reactively—after they are detected or reported—rather than prevented at source. This creates risks of identity theft, unauthorized changes to company records, and governance disputes.  Frequent outages, downtime, and poor performance: Incident logs recorded multiple disruptions between August 2023 and September 2025. Causes included network failures, storage exhaustion, inadequate power backup, system misconfigurations, and human error. These outages locked users out of filing applications. Even when operational, the system often failed to meet approved turnaround times for core services such as company name reservation, business name registration/amendments, and data updates, resulting in delays and inconsistent performance.  Data privacy and protection gaps: Historical business registration records shared with third parties via OBRS contained unredacted sensitive personal information, including full dates of birth of directors, proprietors, and subscribers. This raises cybercrime and identity theft risks in an environment of increasing digital threats.  Inadequate complaint handling and monitoring: URSB did not maintain a comprehensive register of customer complaints related to OBRS. Without tracking complaint types, resolution timelines, or outcomes, the Bureau could not systematically identify recurring problems or measure service quality.  Related project and governance issues: Earlier reviews noted delays against project milestones, lack of formal approval for revised implementation schedules, insufficient monitoring and evaluation of modules during the project lifecycle, and challenges with storage capacity in the early rollout phase. Broader ICT governance weaknesses reported in related coverage included the absence of a formal ICT policy or steering committee, limited internal technical capacity, and heavy reliance on external vendors (including issues around source code control and disaster recovery).  These issues undermined trust in the registry, which is critical for business formalization, investment, banking, and legal processes in Uganda.  Auditor General Recommendations The report urged URSB to: Reduce downtime through better monitoring of storage, power, and network performance, plus redundancy for critical servers. Implement data minimization and redaction of personal information shared externally. Benchmark against other government systems and integrate proper digital signature authentication. Fully implement ISO 9001:2015 quality management standards, including a robust complaints management system.  Subsequent Developments URSB later attained ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management System certification (achieved around December 2025 and publicly celebrated in early 2026), addressing one of the earlier missed deadlines. ) that replaces OBRS. It consolidates business registration, intellectual property, copyright, insolvency, security interest registration, and the Non-Individual Register into a single portal, aiming for improved efficiency, integration, and user experience.In late June 2026, URSB launched a new unified e-Registry platform (accessible ateregistry.ursb.go.ug  Note that some of the allegations in the broader 2026 URSB leadership probe (which led to suspensions and a forensic audit) referenced inflation of ICT system contracts and related governance issues, though these remain under investigation and are distinct from the earlier Auditor General findings on OBRS technical performance.  The Auditor General’s findings represent the most authoritative public assessment of OBRS shortcomings available. Official URSB statements and later upgrades indicate efforts to address reliability and service delivery, but independent verification of post-upgrade performance would require updated audits.  Uganda’s Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) trends, based on Transparency International data, show long-term stagnation in the mid-20s range after a peak in the early 2010s, with a slight recent decline. The CPI scores countries on a 0–100 scale (0 = highly corrupt; 100 = very clean) using expert and business executive assessments of public-sector corruption. Scores are broadly comparable year-to-year since methodological updates around 2012. Recent and historical scores Here is a summary of key data points: Year CPI Score Notes 2025 25 Down 1 point from 2024; rank ~148/182 2024 26 — 2023 26 — 2022 26 — 2021 27 — 2020 27 — 2019 28 Recent high in this period 2018 26 — 2017 26 — 2016 25 — 2015 25 — 2014 26 — 2013 26 — 2012 29 Peak under current methodology Longer-term context (available from ~2001 onward): Average score: ~25. Highest: 29 (2012). Lowest: 19 (2001). Key trends Stagnation after 2012 peak: Scores have hovered mostly between 25 and 28 for over a decade, with no sustained improvement. From 2012 to 2025 the score fell by 4 points overall. Recent decline: After three years of stability at 26 (2022–2024), the 2025 score dropped to 25. Local observers described this as a setback after a period of stagnation. Regional and global comparison: Uganda remains below the Sub-Saharan Africa average (around 32) and the global average (around 42 in recent years). In East Africa it ranks behind peers such as Rwanda (higher scores near 58), Tanzania, and Kenya.  These perception-based scores influence investor confidence, public trust, and assessments of governance risk. Officials and civil society in Uganda have noted the need for stronger anti-corruption measures in response to the persistent low scores. Note that the CPI reflects perceptions rather than a direct count of corruption cases.  Uganda’s investment climate shows relative macroeconomic stability alongside persistent governance and corruption challenges that affect long-term predictability for investors. The recent mandatory leave of five senior Uganda Registration Services Bureau (URSB) officials amid a corruption and mismanagement probe is relevant because URSB handles company/business registration, intellectual property, and related services central to formalization and the ease of doing business.  Macroeconomic backdrop supporting stability Recent data indicate resilience: Growth has been solid (around 6.3% in parts of FY2025/26, with projections in the mid-to-high single digits), supported by domestic demand, oil-related investment, and low inflation (headline/core near 3.4–3.7%, below the Bank of Uganda’s 5% target). FDI has been strong, particularly in oil and gas (record levels reported in recent periods), with foreign reserves building and business confidence indices rising in early-to-mid 2026 despite constraints like competition, weak demand in some sectors, and costs. Oil production is anticipated to begin around late 2026/early FY2026/27, which is expected to further strengthen fiscal and external balances. Authorities and international assessments (IMF, Bank of Uganda) highlight the need for structural reforms—improving the business environment, strengthening governance/anti-corruption frameworks, and enhancing climate resilience—to sustain private-sector-led growth.  Governance and corruption as key risks Corruption remains a structural drag. Uganda’s score on Transparency International’s Corruption Perceptions Index was 25/100 in 2025 (rank around 148 out of 182), reflecting stagnation or slight decline and levels well below regional and global averages. This influences investor perceptions of risk, bureaucratic hurdles, and fair competition.  The U.S. Department of State’s 2025 Investment Climate Statement notes opportunities (market economy, arable land, young population, oil/minerals) but flags corruption, weak rule of law, political risks, and related issues as considerations for investors. Business facilitation involves the Uganda Investment Authority and URSB (often via one-stop approaches), yet practical challenges including delays and informal practices persist. Relevance of the URSB developments URSB is critical to corporate identity, registration processes, and commercial trust. The probe—triggered by internal allegations (including inflated ICT contracts, irregularities in projects/procurement, financial controls, and related issues) and elevated to presidential level—led to mandatory leave for the Registrar General and other senior figures to allow forensic audit without interference. This is not a finding of guilt. Potential positive for stability: High-level intervention can signal seriousness about accountability in a key institution. Transparent resolution, reforms to systems/controls, and sustained service delivery could improve confidence in formal business processes over time.  Near-term considerations: Leadership changes or internal tensions risk temporary disruptions or uncertainty for users of registration services. Prior audits have already noted issues with digital platforms (delays, reliability) despite investments. Overall, macroeconomic indicators currently support a degree of investment climate stability and growth momentum (aided by oil prospects). However, governance weaknesses and perceived corruption continue to constrain deeper confidence and private-sector dynamism. Actions addressing institutional integrity at bodies like URSB, if followed by credible reforms and consistent enforcement, would contribute more meaningfully to longer-term stability than short-term macroeconomic performance alone. International partners consistently emphasize these governance priorities for inclusive, resilient growth.

On May 18, 1980, in Gwangju, there were cases in which citizens raided armories, seized firearms, and rose up in an armed riot. Yet under the pretext of “citizens resisting the military government,” the events were officially designated a “democratization movement” in earnest from 1997 onward.  Even so, among the forces and organizations that pushed for the official “democratization” label, radical leftists clearly existed. Some of them have praised North Korea’s first dictator, Kim Il-sung, while struggling to reject the defense treaty that Korea and the United States maintain on the foundation of free democracy. Generations educated after the founding of the Korean Teachers and Education Workers’ Union (Jeon-gyo-jo) in 1989 were taught that the Gwangju incident is a sacred zone of absolute justice and that the participants resisted for the sake of righteousness. In the early years, children accepted this teaching and fixed in their minds that those involved were absolute justice and an untouchable sacred realm. However, as the information society accelerated from the 2010s onward, younger people began comparing various sources of information with long-standing suspicions. They started to notice facts such as the armed uprising involving firearms, indiscriminate ramming of vehicles into banks in Gwangju, labeling ordinary citizens as spies (ppirakchi), and even torturing and killing some of them.  There have been testimonies that all these actions were justified as “democratization,” and that through their own armed group called the “citizen army,” they surrounded, killed, and harassed citizens who did not cooperate. Nevertheless, they have become “persons of national merit” and enjoy broader benefits than the non-wounded soldiers who participated in the Korean War (the June 25 War). Even their children, amid all this controversy, receive employment preferences and often obtain jobs on a priority basis. Today, South Korea suffers from severe youth unemployment, yet critics point out that these beneficiaries easily secure quality jobs relative to their abilities.  That is not all. Despite enjoying taxpayers’ money and various benefits, they still refuse to make the list of meritorious persons public. If they were truly an absolute sacred realm and had contributed enough to the nation to deserve such benefits through the people’s support, why can they not confidently disclose the list? Radical leftist forces frame ordinary citizens by saying, “The names of the dead are already listed at the national cemetery—why are you so obsessed with publishing the meritorious persons list?” Yet:  It is impossible to cross-check whether those names actually match the list of benefit recipients. Why does the number of 5.18 benefit recipients keep increasing year after year? Why do they refuse a full fact-finding investigation into whether 5.18 is truly a sacred realm?  Even organizations that praise Kim Il-sung—the first dictator of North Korea who starved hundreds of thousands—and his grandson Kim Jong-un call 5.18 a “democratization movement.” Celebrating a democratization movement while praising Kim Jong-un inevitably raises questions and distrust among the public. Recently, Lee Jin-sook, a lawmaker from South Korea’s conservative party, held a forum to examine the facts surrounding the 5.18 events. She was immediately met with calls for her expulsion by the National Assembly Ethics Committee. In contrast, lawmaker Lee Jun-seok, who gathered 600,000 signatures on a national petition calling for his own expulsion, has still received no response from the Assembly regarding expulsion. Is this truly a “free democracy”? Lawmaker Lee Jin-sook spoke only about facts and even proposed a public debate for fact verification. She did not make any denunciatory remarks against the victims. She simply contrasted the commonly held public perception with the available facts. At Lee Jin-sook’s 5.18 forum, a man estimated to be in his 50s caused a disturbance. Even though the lawmaker engaged in no mockery or ridicule, he went into a frenzy over mere “fact comparison.” Many evaluations today say that the student-movement generations of the following decades, including those associated with 5.18, are blocking the path of the younger generation. The reason often cited is that they dominate politics, are concentrated in a particular age group in their 50s, and through radical-left forms are disrupting the order of the market economy and producing results that infringe upon free democracy. Their hypocrisy and the history distorted by that hypocrisy remain powerful. Although young people have opened their eyes, the colored-lens frames instilled through education and culture are still too strong. Young people today often say they hope the day will come when history can be properly criticized and compared. Is the Republic of Korea merely a hollow shell of “free democracy”?

🚨 47 CRYPTO FAILURES. ONE REPEATED WEAKNESS: THE HUMAN LAYER.  A review of 47 crypto security incidents found more than $3.8B lost — and the recurring pattern wasn’t necessarily broken cryptography.  It was people.  Social engineering, compromised developer environments, exposed credentials, weak governance and trusted signers repeatedly became the attacker’s way in.   The lesson for crypto builders is simple:  Don’t design security around trusting the people holding the keys. Design it so compromised people and devices still can’t move the money.  That means simulation, threshold approvals, timelocks, anomaly detection, isolated signing environments and rehearsed incident response.  Your biggest vulnerability may not be your smart contract. Beyond politics: The President’s response to the Kariba tragedy  It is deeply unfortunate that some individuals have chosen to exploit the tragedy at Kariba for cheap political gain rather than allowing the nation to mourn and support the families affected. At a time when the country should be united in grief and compassion, attempts to turn a national tragedy into a political contest are both insensitive and regrettable. Disgraced journalist Hopewell Chin’ono has sought to insinuate, through his social media commentary, that the President of the Republic does not care about the people of Kariba simply because he did not personally attend the funeral proceedings. Such an assertion is misleading and fails to recognise the nature and responsibilities of the Office of the President. Physical presence at every funeral or national event is not the sole measure of a leader’s concern, commitment or compassion.  •Kariba dam accident was declared a national disaster by the President :By formally declaring the Kariba dam incident a national disaster, the President demonstrated that the tragedy was being treated with the seriousness it deserved. Such a declaration is not merely symbolic. It represents the recognition by the highest office in the land that the loss of life has affected families, communities and the nation as a whole, and that Government must mobilise the necessary resources and institutions to respond accordingly. Through this action, the President has made it clear that he mourns with the families and relatives of those who lost their lives.  •The President mourned with the families of the bereaved :It is also common knowledge that the President, like any Head of State and head of government, has the constitutional and administrative authority to delegate responsibilities. Delegation should not be misconstrued as indifference or absence. Effective leadership requires the President to rely on ministers, government officials and other designated representatives to carry out responsibilities on his behalf, particularly when several urgent matters require attention simultaneously.  •Government has been proactive :More importantly, the Government has responded to the tragedy with concrete action. Government institutions and officials have come out in full force to assist the families of the deceased and survivors of the incident. This assistance demonstrates that the Government’s response is not limited to statements of sympathy, but includes practical measures aimed at supporting those directly affected by the disaster. The welfare of citizens must be judged by the actions taken to protect, assist and support them, particularly during moments of profound difficulty. The assistance being provided to the affected families and survivors reflects the Government’s continuing commitment to ensuring that citizens receive support when they need it most and that affected communities are not left to face the consequences of such a tragedy alone.  •Ongoing investigations indicate Government commitment to establish the circumstances surrounding the tragedy :The investigations ordered by the President further demonstrate his direct engagement with the matter. Ordering an investigation is an important step towards establishing the circumstances surrounding the incident, identifying any failures or contributing factors, and ensuring that appropriate lessons are drawn to prevent similar tragedies in the future. It is therefore disingenuous for detractors to suggest that the President is unconcerned when his administration has initiated processes intended to establish the facts and provide accountability. National tragedies should bring citizens together rather than provide opportunities for political point-scoring. The families who lost loved ones deserve dignity, compassion and support, not the exploitation of their grief for political purposes. Survivors deserve assistance, while the nation deserves a clear understanding.

Shadows Over Tomorrow: How Incompetence, Corruption, and Human Rights Failures in Today’s Security Agencies and Police Are Devouring Our Security and Stealing Our Children’s Future In an age of unprecedented technological power and vast resources, our security agencies and police forces should stand as reliable guardians of peace and justice. Instead, they increasingly resemble dysfunctional bureaucracies crippled by incompetence, riddled with corruption, and willing to sacrifice human rights in the name of “security.” The result is not greater safety, but a slow, grinding erosion of the very foundations that keep societies stable. For our children, the horizon looks genuinely dark. Security agencies were created to anticipate threats, protect citizens, and uphold the rule of law. Yet time and again they demonstrate staggering incompetence. Intelligence failures, bloated administrations, and an inability to adapt to modern threats — from sophisticated cybercrime to organized transnational gangs — have become routine. Billions are spent on surveillance systems and counter-terrorism programs, yet ordinary people still feel unsafe in their own neighborhoods. Resources meant for real protection are consumed by internal power struggles, political signaling, and outdated procedures that no longer match the dangers of the 21st century. The public is left paying for agencies that often react too late or not at all. The police, the most visible face of state authority, fare no better. Corruption is not an occasional scandal but a persistent cancer in many forces. Officers and officials have been exposed for taking bribes, planting evidence, protecting criminal networks, and covering up misconduct. Even in countries once admired for institutional integrity, repeated cases of abuse of power and lack of accountability have shattered public trust. When the very people tasked with enforcing the law become part of the problem, the social contract collapses. Citizens stop reporting crimes, stop cooperating with investigations, and begin to view the police as just another threat to navigate rather than a source of protection. Human rights suffer most in this environment. In the pursuit of security, agencies and police forces have normalized practices that trample basic freedoms: mass surveillance that invades private life, discriminatory stop-and-search policies, excessive use of force, and the silencing of dissent under vague “public order” pretexts. International human rights standards are routinely bent or ignored when they become inconvenient. The most vulnerable — young people, minorities, and the economically disadvantaged — bear the heaviest burden. Instead of feeling protected, they learn early that the system views them with suspicion rather than as citizens deserving dignity and safety. The consequences for the next generation are devastating. Children growing up in this reality inherit streets that feel less safe, institutions they cannot trust, and a future in which justice depends more on connections and money than on fairness. When corruption diverts public funds away from schools, youth programs, and community safety, opportunities shrink. When police misconduct and institutional failure breed cynicism, young people lose faith in the possibility of a just society. Mental health struggles, rising youth crime in some areas, and a pervasive sense of insecurity become the new normal. The promise that tomorrow will be better than today rings increasingly hollow. If these patterns continue — if incompetence is rewarded with bigger budgets, if corruption is met with weak accountability, and if human rights are treated as optional extras — the darkness will only deepen. Our children will inherit a world where security is an illusion for the privileged and a distant dream for everyone else. The future does not look merely challenging. It looks compromised at its core. The institutions meant to protect us are failing us.

Stripe's acquisition of #OpenRouter is the largest deal where a fintech company acquires an AI startup, and this deal is the first of its kind  Fintech has been hunting for AI projects for a long time, well before AI became a trend. I analyzed the deals that took place since the emergence of @ChatGPT , and here are the key findings 👇   The OpenRouter acquisition is historical because Stripe bought infrastructure, while every deal before targeted a tool  That is where the money went for four years. Threat detection, fraud prevention, identity. @Visa is one of the most active buyers, acquiring @BioCatch  for $2.4 billion this month and Featurespace for around $935 million in 2024. @Mastercard  set the previous record with @RecordedFuture, AI-powered cyber threat intelligence, at $2.65 billion  @chainalysis, a blockchain intelligence platform, acquired Alterya, a crypto scam detection project, for about $150 million. Socure, a digital identity verification company, paid $136 million for Effectiv, an AI risk decisioning platform built by the team that sold Simility to PayPal.  Banking agentic AI is one of the emerging trends there. Backbase acquired @kasistoinc  AI in June, and @nubank  acquired Hyperplane (acquired by nubank), which builds banking foundation models for personalization and risk.  Others bought their way into better research and back-office decisions. @RobinhoodApp  acquired Pluto Capital for AI investment research, while @tipalti bought Statement, an AI-native treasury forecasting tool.  In my opinion, one of the reasons @stripe  paid an enormous $7B for OpenRouter is that they want to introduce Stripe's product suite to their user base, which is full of tech geeks and business-minded people, specifically their agentic payments stack. What is cybersecurity without networking and networking ? This literally means two different things, and that's why it's important to integrate both in your learning journey. When I say "learning journey," I don't mean just for students, but also for professionals, because we all agree that learning never stops!  I was trying my best to network with people already in the field or fellow enthusiasts like me, so I began searching for cybersecurity events near me. I stumbled upon the @SolutionsPT Cyber Secure OT event, and I was intrigued because I had always heard of IT cybersecurity but couldn't really fathom what OT cybersecurity entailed. I told myself that this was interesting and that I wanted to learn more.  The most interesting part was when I did my research and realized that OT (Operational Technology) cybersecurity is similar to IT (Information Technology) cybersecurity. The main difference is that OT deals with industrial systems and processes, such as manufacturing and utilities, whereas IT focuses on data and information systems. Like IT, OT also uses the cloud to operate. As a cloud enthusiast, I knew it would be beneficial to learn about it.  When I got to the event, I felt lost and confused, with my mind racing with thoughts like "Should I be here?" and "I shouldn't have come." But since I was already there, I decided to face my fear. I got my tea and looked for a stand table to put it on. Everyone seemed occupied at the tables, talking to each other, except for one table where I met a beautiful woman. I approached her and asked if I could share the table with her. She smiled and said yes, and we introduced ourselves.  She mentioned that she didn’t understand the posters about cloud, infrastructure, security, etc. She is a college teacher who wants to integrate cybersecurity into the syllabus but needs to understand more about it. She asked if I understood it, and I confidently said yes. I began explaining in simple terms what cloud security, DMZ, and infrastructure are and how important it is to secure our data. I felt the joy of sharing my knowledge with this amazing woman and it felt like we’ve known each other before the event! (God bless her)  During the event, I learned a lot about OT cybersecurity and how the effects of OT breaches can be more disastrous than IT breaches. For example, while IT breaches might result in data loss or theft, OT breaches can disrupt physical processes, leading to safety hazards and operational shutdowns. One common attack in OT is ransomware, which is especially dangerous because it can halt critical infrastructure, such as power grids or water supply systems, until a ransom is paid.  Additionally, I learned about different devices and AI that can help enhance cybersecurity in OT environments. These devices aid in securing endpoints, detecting malware, and automating policy management. They play a crucial role in maintaining the integrity and security of industrial systems.  A notable OT attack was the 2017 NotPetya ransomware attack, which targeted the Ukrainian power grid. This attack not only disrupted electricity supply to millions of people but also caused widespread chaos, affecting hospitals, transportation systems, and businesses. Such an attack can severely impact everyday life, highlighting the importance of robust cybersecurity measures in OT environments.  By the end of the event, I could identify key points about risk management, OT security and most importantly network with people!  Thanks to all the amazing speakers and organizers!  Facing my fears one demon at a time! Wheew!😑 #Cybersecurity

🇦🇪 UAE: Threat Actor Claims Access to PII of UAE Citizens and Residents  A newly registered threat actor on an underground forum claims to have access to a system capable of retrieving extensive personal information on UAE citizens and residents using an individual's national ID number.  According to the listing, the alleged lookup service can return:  * Full name * Personal photograph * Nationality * Date of birth * Phone number * Email address * Employment information * Passport number, type and expiration date * Additional personal information  The actor is advertising individual lookups for $50 per person and included what appears to be a redacted sample record and photograph as purported evidence.  🔎 Analyst Note: This is currently an unverified threat-actor claim. DDW found no public UAE government disclosure or independent confirmation establishing that a government identity database has been compromised. The screenshot alone does not establish the underlying source of the information or prove the actor has access to "all" UAE citizens and residents.  The claim is nevertheless notable because the UAE's national digital-identity ecosystem uses Emirates ID as a core identifier for citizens and residents. If the advertised access is genuine, identifying the upstream data source would be critical to determining the scope and impact.  #DDW #DarkWeb #UAE #DataBreach #DataLeak #PII #CyberSecurity #ThreatIntelligence

DFAT states that its electronic records are hosted within Australia and protected through measures including secure databases, password protection and MFA. 🚨 OpenAI Expands Daybreak and Introduces GPT-5.6-Cyber for Advanced Cyber Defense  OpenAI has officially announced a major expansion of its Daybreak cybersecurity initiative alongside GPT-5.6-Cyber, its latest cybersecurity-specific model.  * GPT-5.6-Cyber is a purpose-built cybersecurity model based on GPT-5.6 Sol and designed for advanced defensive security work  * OpenAI says GPT-5.6-Cyber completed 95% of requests in its internal advanced cybersecurity evaluation, compared with 1.5% for standard GPT-5.6 Sol  * Daybreak Blue will provide approved defenders access to GPT-5.6 Sol with safeguards specifically designed for authorized defensive cybersecurity work  * Daybreak Red provides vetted security researchers access to purpose-trained cyber models for advanced vulnerability research, exploit validation and security testing  * OpenAI says GPT-5.6-Cyber discovered two previously unknown vulnerabilities in Google's V8 JavaScript engine that could be chained to corrupt memory and escape the V8 heap sandbox  * Google fixed one of the findings as CVE-2026-15903  * OpenAI also reports identifying more than 400 potential privilege-escalation vulnerabilities in a widely used operating-system kernel  * Under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework, GPT-5.6-Cyber has been classified as having High cybersecurity capability while remaining below the company's Critical capability threshold  * OpenAI warns that threat actors will increasingly use AI to conduct cyberattacks at unprecedented speed and scale, potentially including fully autonomous operations  ⚠️ Analyst Note: The significance here extends beyond another cybersecurity-focused AI model. OpenAI is explicitly preparing for a security environment where advanced offensive and defensive cyber capabilities become increasingly automated. ### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 보안 환경은 AI 에이전트의 자율성을 악용하는 공격과 기존 인프라 취약점을 결합한 복합적인 위협이 증가하고 있습니다. 특히 Ray, GitLab, Snowflake 등 오픈소스 및 클라우드 인프라의 취약점을 노린 RCE 공격이 활발하며, 공격자들은 AI를 활용해 공격의 지속성을 확보하고 탐지를 우회하는 전략을 구사하고 있습니다 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/cisa-flags-actively-exploited-ray-flaw.html), [Recorded Future](https://www.recordedfuture.com/blog/hugging-face-cheap-persistence)). 또한, macOS 및 iOS의 WebKit 취약점과 Screen Sharing 기능을 악용한 암호화폐 채굴 캠페인이 지속적으로 보고되고 있어 엔드포인트 보안 강화가 시급합니다 ([SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/dozens-of-webkit-vulnerabilities-patched-with-fresh-macos-ios-security-updates/)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **HoneyMyte**: CoolClient 백도어의 신규 변종을 통해 커널 모드 rootkit을 배포하며 보안 도구 탐지를 우회함 ([Securelist](https://securelist.com/honeymyte-coolclient-driver-rootkit/121028/))
- **Head Mare**: TrueConf 서버 취약점을 악용하여 PhantomCore 및 PhantomGraph 백도어를 배포하는 스파이 활동 수행 ([Securelist](https://securelist.com/tr/head-mare-targets-trueconf-server-with-phantomcore/120988/))
- **Armored Likho**: 기부 캠페인으로 위장하여 Still Toolkit을 배포, Telegram 데이터 탈취 및 도청 시도 ([Securelist](https://securelist.com/armored-likho-still-toolkit/121033/))
- **BlackFile**: 금융 및 의료 기술 조직을 대상으로 하는 랜섬웨어 그룹으로, 최근 다수의 계열사를 통해 강도 높은 금전적 협박 지속 ([CyberScoop](https://cyberscoop.com/blackfile-cyberattacks-financial-sector/))

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **배달 플랫폼 FLY 데이터 유출**: 국내 배달 플랫폼 'FLY'를 대상으로 4,790만 건의 개인정보(주민번호, 계좌, 공동현관 비밀번호 등)가 다크웹 포럼에서 판매 중이라는 주장이 제기됨 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208097))
- **피싱 메일 유포**: AhnLab ASEC은 견적서 확인 및 거래 영수증을 위장한 PhantomStealer 피싱 메일과, 국내 웹 서버를 대상으로 SoftEther VPN을 강제 설치하는 공격 사례를 확인 ([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/94999/), [AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/94994/))
- **티맥스티베로 보안 점검**: 티맥스티베로가 KISA와 협력하여 GPT-5.5-Cyber를 활용한 '티베로7' 보안 정밀 점검 완료 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208100))

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
- **CVE-2025-62593**: Ray-Project Code Injection, CVSS 9.4, KEV 등록 및 악용 확인 ([piyokango](https://twitter.com/piyokango/status/2089484542839296390#m))
- **CVE-2026-8452**: Citrix NetScaler SAML heap overflow, RCE 가능, 공개 PoC 존재 ([ThreatWire_](https://twitter.com/ThreatWire_/status/2089256838495633835#m))
- **CVE-2026-47301**: Microsoft Configuration Manager RCE, SYSTEM 권한 획득 가능, PoC 공개 ([yousukezan](https://twitter.com/yousukezan/status/2089623863571390834#m))

### 5. IOC 요약

- **CVE**: CVE-2025-62593 ([piyokango](https://twitter.com/piyokango/status/2089484542839296390#m)), CVE-2026-8452 ([ThreatWire_](https://twitter.com/ThreatWire_/status/2089256838495633835#m)), CVE-2026-47301 ([yousukezan](https://twitter.com/yousukezan/status/2089623863571390834#m))

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
- **패치 적용**: CISA KEV에 등재된 Ray 취약점 및 Apple(macOS/iOS) 보안 업데이트를 즉시 적용하십시오.
- **엔드포인트 점검**: SoftEther VPN 등 비인가 VPN 설치 여부와 macOS Screen Sharing 활성화 상태를 확인하여 불필요한 원격 접근을 차단하십시오.
- **피싱 대응**: 견적서나 영수증을 사칭한 이메일 첨부파일 실행을 엄격히 금지하고, 조직 내 보안 인식 교육을 강화하십시오.

- **점수**: 8/10
